subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should OpenClaw expose an ordinary plugin runtime caller for plugin-registered Gateway methods, and should that caller be raw dispatch, an allowlisted request API, or a typed service/capability contract?
rationale: This changes the public Plugin SDK and Gateway authorization boundary, so automation cannot safely choose the caller identity, method policy, or permanence of the API.

options.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
options.body: Expose approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

options.title: Keep only the route-scoped helper
options.body: Decline ordinary plugin-to-plugin Gateway calls and require plugins to use existing HTTP route, event, or capability seams.

options.title: Allow raw Gateway dispatch
options.body: Expose a generic method-string caller and accept the broader security and compatibility surface as an explicit product decision.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
recommendation.body: Expose approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced and merged the current route-scoped Gateway method dispatch contract and is the strongest history match for this security boundary decision.
